system.name: Prism
system.one_liner: a cost-efficient multi-LLM serving system that shares GPU memory across models via memory ballooning and flexible space/time sharing

components.name: LLM applications
components.role: the client applications issuing inference requests

components.name: Frontend
components.role: receives inference requests and routes them to the corresponding LLMs

components.name: GPU group 0
components.role: a strict scheduling boundary: a set of GPUs tightly coupled to jointly serve one or more model instances

components.name: GPU group n
components.role: another GPU group, illustrating that multiple groups are managed

components.name: Slack-Aware Request Arbitration
components.role: prioritizes requests on each GPU to maximize SLO attainment

components.name: Model1
components.role: a low-rate model colocated with others via time/space sharing

components.name: Model2
components.role: another low-rate model colocated via time/space sharing

components.name: Model3
components.role: a model colocated in another GPU group via space sharing

components.name: Time Share
components.role: denotes models sharing a GPU by taking turns in time

components.name: Space Share
components.role: denotes models sharing a GPU concurrently by partitioning memory space

components.name: GPU Memory Ballooning
components.role: the balloon-driver mechanism (kvcached) enabling flexible, efficient cross-model memory sharing

components.name: Load-Aware Model Placement
components.role: maximizes memory headroom across GPU groups to facilitate ballooning

content.key_idea: Prism routes requests through a frontend into GPU groups, each a strict scheduling boundary where colocated models share GPUs flexibly via time and space sharing enabled by memory ballooning, coordinated by load-aware placement across groups and slack-aware request arbitration within a group.
content.reading_order: Left to right and top to bottom: LLM applications send Requests into the Frontend, which routes them into GPU group 0 (with its internal Slack-Aware Request Arbitration and Time-Shared Model1/Model2), then down into further GPU groups (..., GPU group n) with Space/Time sharing among Model1/Model2/Model3, with Load-Aware Model Placement annotated as spanning across the groups on the right.

summary: This figure shows the system architecture and design overview of Prism, a cost-efficient multi-LLM serving system. Requests from LLM applications arrive at a Frontend, which routes them into GPU groups -- the strict scheduling boundaries in Prism, each a set of GPUs jointly serving one or more model instances. Within GPU group 0, a Slack-Aware Request Arbitration component prioritizes requests among colocated models (Model1, Model2) that time-share the GPU, underpinned by GPU Memory Ballooning (§5) for flexible cross-model memory sharing. Additional GPU groups (shown as GPU group n) illustrate both time-sharing and space-sharing of models (Model1, Model2, Model3), with Load-Aware Model Placement coordinating model assignment across groups to maximize memory headroom. The diagram is a flat, rounded-box architecture drawing in a blue/orange/pink palette with each mechanism directly annotated by its corresponding paper section number.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Prism 的系统架构：请求经前端路由到各 GPU 组（严格的调度边界），组内模型通过内存气球机制灵活进行时间/空间共享，组内的松弛感知请求仲裁负责优先级调度，负载感知的模型放置则跨多个 GPU 组协调资源分配，图中各机制均标注对应章节号。
notes: Exact section number on the request-arbitration box (read as "§6.3" in the preview image) differs slightly from the body text's "§6.2" reference for slack-aware request arbitration; kept as read from the figure per the labeling rule, but this could be an OCR/reading uncertainty.
